design: plans/cmux-next/chrome-parity/p01-process.md section 2.4 and task p01-process-055. In Chrome's remote_cocoa split the browser process drives RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa in an app shim through RenderWidgetHostNSView and the view answers through RenderWidgetHostNSViewHost. In host mode the Chromium Host is the browser process and cmux's ChromiumHostPageView is the view, so every method of the vendored mojom names its carrier between them. Task p01-process-059 widened it to the remote_cocoa/common mojoms (each file's role says what it carries in Chrome), all vendored at the Chromium revision scripts/cmux-next/cef-manifest.json pins, with each file's commit and sha256, so an upstream change shows as drift; the method and [Sync] counts are parsed from those files. Chrome allows [Sync] calls from the view; cmux has none: what Chrome asks synchronously, the host pushes ahead. scripts/cmux-next/gen-chromium-host-wire.py --check-view-parity checks this file.

mojoms.role: A page's RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa. In host mode the view is cmux's ChromiumHostPageView (055).

Chrome's browser process drives a Views widget's NSWindow (NativeWidgetNSWindowBridge) through it. The Chromium Host keeps every bridge in its own process with the window headless (fork 173, 176): cmux shows a widget's content only as a hosted widget (WIDGET_CONTEXT, 066) or does the widget's job in its own UI (BLOCKED_WIDGET, 068). Calls that only Chrome's browser and dialog windows use need no carrier: cmux never shows those windows.

The NSWindow's side, to the browser. For a hosted widget cmux is the window (cmux_shim_widget_*); for a page the page view's carriers apply. Its [Sync] questions about Chrome's own window chrome have no cmux counterpart, and cmux asks none.
